sanskrit_shloka:
सुवर्णाज्जायमानस्य सुवर्णत्वं च शाश्वतम्।
ब्रह्मणो जायमानस्य ब्रह्मत्वं च तथा भवेत्।।51।।
transliteration:
Suvarṇājjāyamānasya suvarṇatvaṃ ca śāśvatam.
Brahmaṇo jāyamānasya brahmatvaṃ ca tathā bhavet..51..
translation: Just as a thing made of gold ever has the nature of gold, so also a being born of Brahman has always the nature of Brahman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as a thing made of gold ever has the nature of gold, so also a being born of Brahman has always the nature of Brahman.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्वल्पमप्यन्तरं कृत्वा जीवात्मपरमात्मनोः।
योऽवतिष्ठति मूढात्मा भयं तस्याभिभाषितम्।।52।।
transliteration:
Svalpamapyantaraṃ kṛtvā jīvātmaparamātmanoḥ.
Yo'vatiṣṭhati mūḍhātmā bhayaṃ tasyābhibhāṣitam..52..
translation: Fear is attributed to the ignorant one who rests after making even the slightest distinction between the Jivatman and the Paramatman.

word_by_word.word_english: individual soul | paramātmanoḥ:of the Supreme Soul);

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Fear is attributed to the ignorant one who rests after making even the slightest distinction between the Jivatman and the Paramatman.

sanskrit_shloka:
यत्राज्ञानाद्भवेद्द्वैतमितरस्तत्र पश्यति।
आत्मत्वेन यदा सर्वं नेतरस्तत्र चाण्वपि।।53।।
transliteration:
Yatrājñānādbhaveddvaitamitarastatra paśyati.
Ātmatvena yadā sarvaṃ netarastatra cāṇvapi..53..
translation: When duality appears through ignorance, one sees another; but when everything becomes identified with the Atman, one does not perceive another even in the least.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When duality appears through ignorance, one sees another; but when everything becomes identified with the Atman, one does not perceive another even in the least.

sanskrit_shloka:
यस्मिन्सर्वाणि भूतानि ह्यात्मत्वेन विजानतः।
न वै तस्य भवेन्मोहो न च शोकोऽद्वितीयतः।।54।।
transliteration:
Yasminsarvāṇi bhūtāni hyātmatvena vijānataḥ.
Na vai tasya bhavenmoho na ca śoko'dvitīyataḥ..54..
translation: In that state when one realizes all as identified with the Atman, there arises neither delusion nor sorrow, in consequence of the absence of duality.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: In that state when one realizes all as identified with the Atman, there arises neither delusion nor sorrow, in consequence of the absence of duality.

sanskrit_shloka:
अयमात्मा हि ब्रह्मैव सर्वात्मकतया स्थितः।
इति निर्धारितं श्रुत्या बृहदारण्यसंस्थया।।55।।
transliteration:
Ayamātmā hi brahmaiva sarvātmakatayā sthitaḥ.
Iti nirdhāritaṃ śrutyā bṛhadāraṇyasaṃsthayā..55..
translation: The Shruti in the form of the Brihadaranyaka has declared that this Atman, which is the Self of all, is verily Brahman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Shruti in the form of the Brihadaranyaka has declared that this Atman, which is the Self of all, is verily Brahman.

sanskrit_shloka:
अनुभूतोऽप्ययं लोको व्यवहारक्षमोऽपि सन्।
असद्रूपो यथा स्वप्न उत्तरक्षणबाधतः।।56।।
transliteration:
Anubhūto'pyayaṃ loko vyavahārakṣamo'pi san.
Asadrūpo yathā svapna uttarakṣaṇabādhataḥ..56..
translation: This world, though an object of our daily experience and serving all practical purposes, is, like the dream world, of the nature of non-existence, inasmuch as it is contradicted the next moment.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: This world, though an object of our daily experience and serving all practical purposes, is, like the dream world, of the nature of non-existence, inasmuch as it is contradicted the next moment.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्वप्नो जागरणेऽलीकः स्वप्नेऽपि न हि जागरः।
द्वयमेव लये नास्ति लयोऽपि ह्युभयोर्न च।।57।।
transliteration:
Svapno jāgaraṇe'līkaḥ svapne'pi na hi jāgaraḥ.
Dvayameva laye nāsti layo'pi hyubhayorna ca..57..
translation: The dream (experience) is unreal in waking, whereas the waking (experience) is absent in dream. Both, however, are non-existent in deep sleep which, again, is not experienced in either.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The dream (experience) is unreal in waking, whereas the waking (experience) is absent in dream. Both, however, are non-existent in deep sleep which, again, is not experienced in either.

sanskrit_shloka:
त्रयमेवं भवेन्मिथ्या गुणत्रयविनिर्मितम्।
अस्य द्रष्टा गुणातीतो नित्यो ह्येकश्चिदात्मकः।।58।।
transliteration:
Trayamevaṃ bhavenmithyā guṇatrayavinirmitam.
Asya draṣṭā guṇātīto nityo hyekaścidātmakaḥ..58..
translation: Thus all the three states are unreal inasmuch as they are the creation of the three Gunas; but their witness (the reality behind them) is, beyond all Gunas, eternal, one, and is Consciousness itself.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Thus all the three states are unreal inasmuch as they are the creation of the three Gunas; but their witness (the reality behind them) is, beyond all Gunas, eternal, one, and is Consciousness itself.

sanskrit_shloka:
यद्वन्मृदि घटभ्रान्तिं शुक्तौ वा रजतस्थितिम्।
तद्वद्ब्रह्मणि जीवत्वं भ्रान्त्या पश्यति न स्वतः।।59।।
transliteration:
Yadvanmṛdi ghaṭabhrāntiṃ śuktau vā rajatasthitim.
Tadvadbrahmaṇi jīvatvaṃ bhrāntyā paśyati na svataḥ..59..
translation: Just as (after the illusion has gone) one is no more deluded to see a jar in earth or silver in the nacre, so does one no more see Jiva in Brahman when the latter is realized (as one's own self).

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as (after the illusion has gone) one is no more deluded to see a jar in earth or silver in the nacre, so does one no more see Jiva in Brahman when the latter is realized (as one's own self).

sanskrit_shloka:
यथा मृदि घटो नाम कनके कुण्डलाभिधा।
शुक्तौ हि रजतख्यातिर्जीवशब्दस्तथा परे।।60।।
transliteration:
Yathā mṛdi ghaṭo nāma kanake kuṇḍalābhidhā.
Śuktau hi rajatakhyātirjīvaśabdastathā pare..60..
translation: Just as earth is described as a jar, gold as an ear-ring, and a nacre as silver, so is Brahman described as Jiva.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as earth is described as a jar, gold as an ear-ring, and a nacre as silver, so is Brahman described as Jiva.

sanskrit_shloka:
यथैव व्योम्नि नीलत्वं यथा नीरं मरुस्थले।
पुरुषत्वं यथा स्थाणौ तद्वद्विश्वं चिदात्मनि।।61।।
transliteration:
Yathaiva vyomni nīlatvaṃ yathā nīraṃ marusthale.
Puruṣatvaṃ yathā sthāṇau tadvadviśvaṃ cidātmani..61..
translation: Just as blueness in the sky, water in the mirage, and a human figure in a post (are but illusory), so is the universe in Atman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as blueness in the sky, water in the mirage, and a human figure in a post (are but illusory), so is the universe in Atman.

sanskrit_shloka:
यथैव शून्ये वेतालो गन्धर्वाणां पुरं यथा।
यथाकाशे द्विचन्द्रत्वं तद्वत्सत्ये जगत्स्थितिः।।62।।
transliteration:
Yathaiva śūnye vetālo gandharvāṇāṃ puraṃ yathā.
Yathākāśe dvicandratvaṃ tadvatsatye jagatsthitiḥ..62..
translation: Just as the appearance of a ghost in an empty place, of a castle in the air, and of a second moon in the sky (is illusory), so is the appearance of the universe in Brahman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as the appearance of a ghost in an empty place, of a castle in the air, and of a second moon in the sky (is illusory), so is the appearance of the universe in Brahman.

sanskrit_shloka:
यथा तरङ्गकल्लोलैर्जलमेव स्फुरत्यलम्।
पात्ररूपेण ताम्रं हि ब्रह्माण्डौघैस्तथात्मता।।63।।
transliteration:
Yathā taraṅgakallolairjalameva sphuratyalam.
Pātrarūpeṇa tāmraṃ hi brahmāṇḍaughaistathātmatā..63..
translation: Just as it is water that appears as ripples and waves, or again it is copper, that appears in the form of vessel so it is Atman that appears as the whole universe.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as it is water that appears as ripples and waves, or again it is copper, that appears in the form of vessel so it is Atman that appears as the whole universe.

sanskrit_shloka:
घटनाम्ना यथा पृथ्वी पटनाम्ना हि तन्तवः।
जगन्नाम्ना चिदाभाति ज्ञेयं तत्तदभावतः।।64।।
transliteration:
Ghaṭanāmnā yathā pṛthvī paṭanāmnā hi tantavaḥ.
Jagannāmnā cidābhāti jñeyaṃ tattadabhāvataḥ..64..
translation: Just as it is earth that appears under the name of a jar, or it is threads that appear under the name of a cloth, so it is Atman that appears under the name of the universe. This Atman is to be known by negating the names.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as it is earth that appears under the name of a jar, or it is threads that appear under the name of a cloth, so it is Atman that appears under the name of the universe. This Atman is to be known by negating the names.

sanskrit_shloka:
सर्वोऽपि व्यवहारस्तु ब्रह्मणा क्रियते जनैः।
अज्ञानान्न विजानन्ति मृदेव हि घटादिकम्।।65।।
transliteration:
Sarvo'pi vyavahārastu brahmaṇā kriyate janaiḥ.
Ajñānānna vijānanti mṛdeva hi ghaṭādikam..65..
translation: People perform all their actions in and through Brahman, (but on account of ignorance they are not aware of that), just as through ignorance persons do not know that jars and other earthenwares are nothing but earth.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: People perform all their actions in and through Brahman, (but on account of ignorance they are not aware of that), just as through ignorance persons do not know that jars and other earthenwares are nothing but earth.

sanskrit_shloka:
कार्यकारणता नित्यमास्ते घटमृदोर्यथा।
तथैव श्रुतियुक्तिभ्यां प्रपञ्चब्रह्मणोरिह।।66।।
transliteration:
Kāryakāraṇatā nityamāste ghaṭamṛdoryathā.
Tathaiva śrutiyuktibhyāṃ prapañcabrahmaṇoriha..66..
translation: Just as there ever exist the relation of cause and effect between earth and a jar, so does the same relation exist between Brahman and the phenomenal world; this has been established here on the strength of scriptural texts and reasoning.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as there ever exist the relation of cause and effect between earth and a jar, so does the same relation exist between Brahman and the phenomenal world; this has been established here on the strength of scriptural texts and reasoning.

sanskrit_shloka:
गृह्यमाणे घटे यद्वन्मृत्तिका भाति वै बलात्।
वीक्ष्यमाणे प्रपञ्चेऽपि ब्रह्मैवाभाति भासुरम्।।67।।
transliteration:
Gṛhyamāṇe ghaṭe yadvanmṛttikā bhāti vai balāt.
Vīkṣyamāṇe prapañce'pi brahmaivābhāti bhāsuram..67..
translation: Just as (the consciousness of) earth forces itself upon our mind while thinking of a jar, so also does (the idea of) ever-shining Brahman flash on us while contemplating on the phenomenal world.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as (the consciousness of) earth forces itself upon our mind while thinking of a jar, so also does (the idea of) ever-shining Brahman flash on us while contemplating on the phenomenal world.

sanskrit_shloka:
सदैवात्मा विशुद्धोऽपि ह्यशुद्धो भाति वै सदा।
यथैव द्विविधा रज्जुर्ज्ञानिनोऽज्ञानिनोऽनिशम्।।68।।
transliteration:
Sadaivātmā viśuddho'pi hyaśuddho bhāti vai sadā.
Yathaiva dvividhā rajjurjñānino'jñānino'niśam..68..
translation: Atman, though ever pure (to a wise man), always appears to be impure (to an ignorant one), just as a rope always appears in two different ways to a knowing person and an ignorant one.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Atman, though ever pure (to a wise man), always appears to be impure (to an ignorant one), just as a rope always appears in two different ways to a knowing person and an ignorant one.

sanskrit_shloka:
यथैव मृन्मयः कुम्भस्तद्वद्देहोऽपि चिन्मयः।
आत्मानात्मविभागोऽयं मुधैव क्रियते बुधैः।।69।।
transliteration:
Yathaiva mṛnmayaḥ kumbhastadvaddeho'pi cinmayaḥ.
Ātmānātmavibhāgo'yaṃ mudhaiva kriyate budhaiḥ..69..
translation: Just as a jar is all earth, so also is the body all consciousness. The division, therefore, into the Self and non-Self is made by the ignorant to no purpose.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as a jar is all earth, so also is the body all consciousness. The division, therefore, into the Self and non-Self is made by the ignorant to no purpose.

sanskrit_shloka:
सर्पत्वेन यथा रज्जू रजतत्वेन शुक्तिका।
विनिर्णीता विमूढेन देहत्वेन तथात्मता।।70।।
transliteration:
Sarpatvena yathā rajjū rajatatvena śuktikā.
Vinirṇītā vimūḍhena dehatvena tathātmatā..70..
translation: Just as a rope is imagined to be a snake and a nacre to be a piece of silver, so is the Atman determined to be the body by an ignorant person.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as a rope is imagined to be a snake and a nacre to be a piece of silver, so is the Atman determined to be the body by an ignorant person.

sanskrit_shloka:
घटत्वेन यथा पृथ्वी पटत्वेनैव तन्तवः।
विनिर्णीता विमूढेन देहत्वेन तथात्मता।।71।।
transliteration:
Ghaṭatvena yathā pṛthvī paṭatvenaiva tantavaḥ.
Vinirṇītā vimūḍhena dehatvena tathātmatā..71..
translation: Just as earth is thought of as a jar (made of it) and threads as a cloth, so is Atman, etc.,

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as earth is thought of as a jar (made of it) and threads as a cloth, so is Atman, etc.,

sanskrit_shloka:
कनकं कुण्डलत्वेन तरङ्गत्वेन वै जलम्।
विनिर्णीता विमूढेन देहत्वेन तथात्मता।।72।।
transliteration:
Kanakaṃ kuṇḍalatvena taraṅgatvena vai jalam.
Vinirṇītā vimūḍhena dehatvena tathātmatā..72..
translation: Just as gold is thought of as an ear-ring and water as waves, so is the Atman, etc.,

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as gold is thought of as an ear-ring and water as waves, so is the Atman, etc.,

sanskrit_shloka:
पुरुषत्वेन वै स्थाणुर्जलत्वेन मरीचिका।
विनिर्णीता विमूढेन देहत्वेन तथात्मता।।73।।
transliteration:
Puruṣatvena vai sthāṇurjalatvena marīcikā.
Vinirṇītā vimūḍhena dehatvena tathātmatā..73..
translation: Just as the stump of a tree is mistaken for a human figure and a mirage for water, so is the Atman, etc.,

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as the stump of a tree is mistaken for a human figure and a mirage for water, so is the Atman, etc.,

sanskrit_shloka:
गृहत्वेनैव काष्ठानि खङ्गत्वेनैव लोहता।
विनिर्णीता विमूढेन देहत्वेन तथात्मता।।74।।
transliteration:
Gṛhatvenaiva kāṣṭhāni khaṅgatvenaiva lohatā.
Vinirṇītā vimūḍhena dehatvena tathātmatā..74..
translation: Just as a mass of wood work is thought of as a house and iron as a sword, so is the Atman, etc.,

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as a mass of wood work is thought of as a house and iron as a sword, so is the Atman, etc.,

sanskrit_shloka:
यथा वृक्षविपर्यासो जलाद्भवति कस्यचित्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।75।।
transliteration:
Yathā vṛkṣaviparyāso jalādbhavati kasyacit.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..75..
translation: Just as one sees the illusion of a tree on account of water, so does a person on account of ignorance see Atman as the body.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as one sees the illusion of a tree on account of water, so does a person on account of ignorance see Atman as the body.

sanskrit_shloka:
पोतेन गच्छतः पुंसः सर्वं भातीव चञ्चलम्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।76।।
transliteration:
Potena gacchataḥ puṃsaḥ sarvaṃ bhātīva cañcalam.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..76..
translation: Just as to a person going in a boat everything appears to be in motion, so does one, etc.,

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as to a person going in a boat everything appears to be in motion, so does one, etc.,

sanskrit_shloka:
पीतत्वं हि यथा शुभ्रे दोषाद्भवति कस्यचित्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।77।।
transliteration:
Pītatvaṃ hi yathā śubhre doṣādbhavati kasyacit.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..77..
translation: Just as to a person suffering from a defect (jaundice) white things appear as yellow, so does one, etc.,

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as to a person suffering from a defect (jaundice) white things appear as yellow, so does one, etc.,

sanskrit_shloka:
चक्षुर्भ्यां भ्रमशीलाभ्यां सर्वं भाति भ्रमात्मकम्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।78।।
transliteration:
Cakṣurbhyāṃ bhramaśīlābhyāṃ sarvaṃ bhāti bhramātmakam.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..78..
translation: Just as to a person with defective eyes everything appears to be defective, so does one, etc.,

word_by_word.word_english: delusion | śīlābhyām:by the ones with nature);

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as to a person with defective eyes everything appears to be defective, so does one, etc.,

sanskrit_shloka:
अलातं भ्रमणेनैव वर्तुलं भाति सूर्यवत्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।79।।
transliteration:
Alātaṃ bhramaṇenaiva vartulaṃ bhāti sūryavat.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..79..
translation: Just as a firebrand, through mere rotation, appears circular like the sun, so does one, etc.,

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as a firebrand, through mere rotation, appears circular like the sun, so does one, etc.,

sanskrit_shloka:
महत्त्वे सर्ववस्तूनामणुत्वं ह्यतिदूरतः।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।80।।
transliteration:
Mahattve sarvavastūnāmaṇutvaṃ hyatidūrataḥ.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..80..
translation: Just as all things that are really large appear to be very small owing to great distance, so does one, etc.,

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as all things that are really large appear to be very small owing to great distance, so does one, etc.,

sanskrit_shloka:
सूक्ष्मत्वे सर्ववस्तूनां स्थूलत्वं चोपनेत्रतः।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।81।।
transliteration:
Sūkṣmatve sarvavastūnāṃ sthūlatvaṃ copanetrataḥ.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..81..
translation: Just as all objects that are very small appear to be large when viewed through lenses, so does one, etc.,

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as all objects that are very small appear to be large when viewed through lenses, so does one, etc.,

sanskrit_shloka:
काचभूमौ जलत्वं वा जलभूमौ हि काचता।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।82।।
transliteration:
Kācabhūmau jalatvaṃ vā jalabhūmau hi kācatā.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..82..
translation: Just as a surface of glass is mistaken for water, or vice versa, so does one, etc.,

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as a surface of glass is mistaken for water, or vice versa, so does one, etc.,

sanskrit_shloka:
यद्वदग्नौ मणित्वं हि मणौ वा वह्निता पुमान्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।83।।
transliteration:
Yadvadagnau maṇitvaṃ hi maṇau vā vahnitā pumān.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..83..
translation: Just as a person imagines a jewel in fire or vice versa, so does one, etc.,

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as a person imagines a jewel in fire or vice versa, so does one, etc.,

sanskrit_shloka:
अभ्रेषु सत्सु धावत्सु धावन्निव यथा शशी।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।84।।
transliteration:
Abhreṣu satsu dhāvatsu dhāvanniva yathā śaśī.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..84..
translation: Just as when clouds move, the moon appears to be in motion, so does one, etc.,

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as when clouds move, the moon appears to be in motion, so does one, etc.,

sanskrit_shloka:
यथैव दिग्विपर्यासो मोहाद्भवति कस्यचित्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।85।।
transliteration:
Yathaiva digviparyāso mohādbhavati kasyacit.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..85..
translation: Just as a person through confusion loses all distinction between the different points of the compass, so does one, etc.,

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as a person through confusion loses all distinction between the different points of the compass, so does one, etc.,

sanskrit_shloka:
यथा शशी जले भाति चञ्चलत्वेन कस्यचित्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।86।।
transliteration:
Yathā śaśī jale bhāti cañcalatvena kasyacit.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..86..
translation: Just as the moon (when reflected) in water appears to one as unsteady, so does one, etc.,

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as the moon (when reflected) in water appears to one as unsteady, so does one, etc.,

sanskrit_shloka:
एवमात्मनि नज्ञाते देहाध्यासो हि जायते।
स एवात्मा परिज्ञातो लीयते च परात्मनि।।87।।
transliteration:
Evamātmani najñāte dehādhyāso hi jāyate.
Sa evātmā parijñāto līyate ca parātmani..87..
translation: Thus through ignorance arises in Atman the delusion of the body, which, again, through Self-realization, disappears in the supreme Atman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Thus through ignorance arises in Atman the delusion of the body, which, again, through Self-realization, disappears in the supreme Atman.

sanskrit_shloka:
सर्वमात्मतया ज्ञातं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम्।
अभावात्सर्वभावानां देहानां चात्मता कुतः।।88।।
transliteration:
Sarvamātmatayā jñātaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam.
Abhāvātsarvabhāvānāṃ dehānāṃ cātmatā kutaḥ..88..
translation: When the whole universe, movable and immovable, is known to be Atman, and thus the existence of everything else is negated, where is then any room to say that the body is Atman?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When the whole universe, movable and immovable, is known to be Atman, and thus the existence of everything else is negated, where is then any room to say that the body is Atman?

sanskrit_shloka:
आत्मानं सततं जानन्कालं नय महामते।
प्रारब्धमखिलं भुञ्जन्नोद्वेगं कर्तुमर्हसि।।89।।
transliteration:
Ātmānaṃ satataṃ jānankālaṃ naya mahāmate.
Prārabdhamakhilaṃ bhuñjannodvegaṃ kartumarhasi..89..
translation: O enlightened one, pass your time always contemplating on Atman while you are experiencing all the results of Prarabdha; for it ill becomes you to feel distressed.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: O enlightened one, pass your time always contemplating on Atman while you are experiencing all the results of Prarabdha; for it ill becomes you to feel distressed.

sanskrit_shloka:
उत्पन्नेऽप्यात्मविज्ञाने प्रारब्धं नैव मुञ्चति।
इति यच्छ्रूयते शास्त्रात्तन्निराक्रियतेऽधुना।।90।।
transliteration:
Utpanne'pyātmavijñāne prārabdhaṃ naiva muñcati.
Iti yacchrūyate śāstrāttannirākriyate'dhunā..90..
translation: The theory one hears of from the scripture, that Prarabdha does not lose its hold upon one even after the origination of the knowledge of Atman, is now being refuted.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The theory one hears of from the scripture, that Prarabdha does not lose its hold upon one even after the origination of the knowledge of Atman, is now being refuted.

sanskrit_shloka:
तत्त्वज्ञानोदयादूर्ध्वं प्रारब्धं नैव विद्यते।
देहादीनामसत्यत्वाद्यथा स्वप्नः प्रबोधतः।।91।।
transliteration:
Tattvajñānodayādūrdhvaṃ prārabdhaṃ naiva vidyate.
Dehādīnāmasatyatvādyathā svapnaḥ prabodhataḥ..91..
translation: After the origination of the knowledge of Reality, Prarabdha verily ceases to exist, inasmuch as the body and the like become non-existent; just as a dream does not exist on waking.

word_by_word.word_sanskrit: – from the rise of true knowledge (tattva

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: After the origination of the knowledge of Reality, Prarabdha verily ceases to exist, inasmuch as the body and the like become non-existent; just as a dream does not exist on waking.

sanskrit_shloka:
कर्म जन्मान्तरकृतं प्रारब्धमिति कीर्तितम्।
तत्तु जन्मान्तराभावात्पुंसो नैवास्ति कर्हिचित्।।92।।
transliteration:
Karma janmāntarakṛtaṃ prārabdhamiti kīrtitam.
Tattu janmāntarābhāvātpuṃso naivāsti karhicit..92..
translation: That Karma which is done in a previous life is known as Prarabdha (which produces the present life). But such Karma cannot take the place of Prarabdha (for a man of knowledge), as he has no other birth (being free from ego).

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That Karma which is done in a previous life is known as Prarabdha (which produces the present life). But such Karma cannot take the place of Prarabdha (for a man of knowledge), as he has no other birth (being free from ego).

sanskrit_shloka:
स्वप्नदेहो यथाध्यस्तस्तथैवायं हि देहकः।।
अध्यस्तस्य कुतो जन्म जन्माभावे स्थितिः कुतः।।93।।
transliteration:
Svapnadeho yathādhyastastathaivāyaṃ hi dehakaḥ..
Adhyastasya kuto janma janmābhāve sthitiḥ kutaḥ..93..
translation: Just as the body in a dream is superimposed (and therefore illusory), so is also this body. How could there be any birth of the superimposed (body), and in the absence of birth (of the body) where is the room for that (i.e., Prarabdha) at all ?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as the body in a dream is superimposed (and therefore illusory), so is also this body. How could there be any birth of the superimposed (body), and in the absence of birth (of the body) where is the room for that (i.e., Prarabdha) at all ?

sanskrit_shloka:
उपादानं प्रपञ्चस्य मृद्भाण्डस्येव कथ्यते।
अज्ञानं चैव वेदान्तैस्तस्मिन्नष्टे क्व विश्वता।।94।।
transliteration:
Upādānaṃ prapañcasya mṛdbhāṇḍasyeva kathyate.
Ajñānaṃ caiva vedāntaistasminnaṣṭe kva viśvatā..94..
translation: The Vedanta texts declare ignorance to be verily the material (cause) of the phenomenal world just as earth is of a jar. That (ignorance) being destroyed, where can the universe subsist ?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Vedanta texts declare ignorance to be verily the material (cause) of the phenomenal world just as earth is of a jar. That (ignorance) being destroyed, where can the universe subsist ?

sanskrit_shloka:
यथा रज्जुं परित्यज्य सर्प गृह्णाति वै भ्रमात्।
तद्वत्सत्यमविज्ञाय जगत्पश्यति मूढधीः।।95।।
transliteration:
Yathā rajjuṃ parityajya sarpa gṛhṇāti vai bhramāt.
Tadvatsatyamavijñāya jagatpaśyati mūḍhadhīḥ..95..
translation: Just as a person out of confusion perceives only the snake leaving aside the rope, so does an ignorant person see only the phenomenal world without knowing the reality.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as a person out of confusion perceives only the snake leaving aside the rope, so does an ignorant person see only the phenomenal world without knowing the reality.

sanskrit_shloka:
रज्जुरूपे परिज्ञाते सर्पभ्रान्तिर्न तिष्ठति।
अधिष्ठाने तथा ज्ञाते प्रपञ्चः शून्यतां व्रजेत्।।96।।
transliteration:
Rajjurūpe parijñāte sarpabhrāntirna tiṣṭhati.
Adhiṣṭhāne tathā jñāte prapañcaḥ śūnyatāṃ vrajet..96..
translation: The real nature of the rope being known, the appearance of the snake no longer persists; so the substratum being known, the phenomenal world disappears completely.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The real nature of the rope being known, the appearance of the snake no longer persists; so the substratum being known, the phenomenal world disappears completely.

sanskrit_shloka:
देहस्यापि प्रपञ्चत्वात्प्रारब्धावस्थितिः कुतः।
अज्ञानिजनबोधार्थं प्रारब्धं वक्ति वै श्रुतिः।।97।।
transliteration:
Dehasyāpi prapañcatvātprārabdhāvasthitiḥ kutaḥ.
Ajñānijanabodhārthaṃ prārabdhaṃ vakti vai śrutiḥ..97..
translation: The body also being within the phenomenal world (and therefore unreal), how could Prarabdha exist ? It is, therefore, for the understanding of the ignorant alone that the Shruti speaks of Prarabdha.

word_by_word.word_english: ignorant people | jana:people | bodha:understanding | artham:for the purpose of);

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The body also being within the phenomenal world (and therefore unreal), how could Prarabdha exist ? It is, therefore, for the understanding of the ignorant alone that the Shruti speaks of Prarabdha.

sanskrit_shloka:
क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन्दृष्टे परावरे।
बहुत्वं तन्निषेधार्थं श्रुत्या गीतं च वै स्फुटम्।।98।।
transliteration:
Kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmindṛṣṭe parāvare.
Bahutvaṃ tanniṣedhārthaṃ śrutyā gītaṃ ca vai sphuṭam..98..
translation: "And all the actions of a man perish when he realizes that (Atman) which is both the higher and the lower". Here the clear use of the plural by the Shruti is to negate Prarabdha as well.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: "And all the actions of a man perish when he realizes that (Atman) which is both the higher and the lower". Here the clear use of the plural by the Shruti is to negate Prarabdha as well.

sanskrit_shloka:
उच्यतेऽज्ञैर्बलाच्चैतत्तदानर्थद्वयागमः।
वेदान्तमतहानं च यतो ज्ञानमिति श्रुतिः।।99।।
transliteration:
Ucyate'jñairbalāccaitattadānarthadvayāgamaḥ.
Vedāntamatahānaṃ ca yato jñānamiti śrutiḥ..99..
translation: If the ignorant still arbitrarily maintain this, they will not only involve themselves into two absurdities but will also run the risk of forgoing the Vedantic conclusion. So one should accept those Shrutis alone from which proceeds true knowledge.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: If the ignorant still arbitrarily maintain this, they will not only involve themselves into two absurdities but will also run the risk of forgoing the Vedantic conclusion. So one should accept those Shrutis alone from which proceeds true knowledge.

sanskrit_shloka:
त्रिपञ्चाङ्गान्यथो वक्ष्ये पूर्वोक्तस्यैव सिद्धये।
तैश्च सर्वैः सदा कार्यं निदिध्यासनमेव तु।।100।।
transliteration:
Tripañcāṅgānyatho vakṣye pūrvoktasyaiva siddhaye.
Taiśca sarvaiḥ sadā kāryaṃ nididhyāsanameva tu..100..
translation: Now, for the attainment of the aforesaid (knowledge), I shall expound the fifteen steps by the help of which one should practice profound meditation at all times.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Now, for the attainment of the aforesaid (knowledge), I shall expound the fifteen steps by the help of which one should practice profound meditation at all times.
